MovingVehicle.Operation reported the carriage-for-hire case as not prohibited (`Prohibited: false` for `Prohibited: true` in the branch for it), so an operation the exception cannot excuse resolved permitted; this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`).

MovingVehicle.Operation answered the open question instead of declining: the final decline was replaced by `Resolution<MovingVehicleFinding>.FromValue(new MovingVehicleFinding(fromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle, transportingAnotherPersonsPropertyForCompensationOrHire, Prohibited: false, waiver))`, the plausible reading that a sparsely populated area may be presumed, so the case the map leaves open resolved permitted; this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`). It went red too with the reason wrong (`UnresolvedReason.UnsupportedRule` for `UnresolvedReason.RequiresInterpretation`). Citing moving-aircraft-operation's locator (`MapEntries.MovingAircraftOperation.Locator` for `MapEntries.MovingVehicleOperation.Locator`) did NOT turn it red: both entries cite § 107.25, the consequence decision 0001 records for the two § 107.51(a) entries, so Attempted naming the entry is what distinguishes them and this test asserts it.

MovingVehicle.Operation handed the gate a statement that no waiver is in force (`waiver with { InForce = false }` for `waiver`), so a stated waiver was not honoured and the entry answered a verdict; this test went red (`Failed: 2, Passed: 6`, with the other waiver test). It went red too with MovingVehicle.Operation naming moving-aircraft-operation as the suspended entry (`MapEntries.MovingAircraftOperation` for `MapEntries.MovingVehicleOperation`), so Attempted named the other § 107.25 entry rather than this one.

MovingVehicle.Operation evaluated § 107.205(a)'s proviso, running the gate only when nothing is carried for hire (`if (!transportingAnotherPersonsPropertyForCompensationOrHire && Waivers.Suspension(...) is { } suspended)` for `if (Waivers.Suspension(...) is { } suspended)`), so a stated waiver plus carriage for hire resolved prohibited instead of declining, which is the reading waivable-regulations' note rules out — the provisos "are not evaluated"; this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`) and the other waiver test stayed green, so the gate's place before the verdict is what it pins.

Handlers.MovingVehicleOperation defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(MovingVehicle.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, ...)`); this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`).

Handlers.MovingVehicleOperation defaulted the unstated vehicle fact to false (`request.FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle ?? false` for `Demand(request.FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle, ...)`), so the engine inferred that the operation was not from a moving vehicle; this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`). It went red too with the carriage fact defaulted the same way (`request.TransportingAnotherPersonsPropertyForCompensationOrHire ?? false` for its `Demand(...)`), so the engine inferred the commercial character of the flight.

MovingVehicle.Operation compared the statement's regulation with itself (`waiver.Regulation` for `Regulation` in the call to Waivers.Suspension), so a waiver of § 107.51 suspended § 107.25; this test went red (`Failed: 1, Passed: 7`).

`Handlers.MovingVehicleOperation` demanded the typed input ahead of the rule's § 107.205 gate -- the ordering thirteen of the fifteen gated entries took before #93 -- by wrapping the argument back up (`Demand(request.FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle, request.EntryId, nameof(request.FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle))` for `request.FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle`). A caller stating a certificate of waiver of § 107.25 in force and describing nothing else was then refused `ArgumentException` naming `FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle` -- `FactRequired`, `MissingInput=FromMovingLandOrWaterBorneVehicle`, filed under `Outstanding`, which `OperationEvaluation.Outstanding` documents as "everything the caller still owes this engine" -- instead of being declined `OutsideCurrentScope` citing § 107.205 (`docs/decisions/0008-the-waiver-gate-precedes-every-other-demand.md`).
